title: August and the Signal
premise: Rosalind Amberdale, a clone carrying her original's memories and unsolved murder, hauls cargo along the silent route between the outer colonies and an Earth that stopped answering years ago. When gravity stutters for nine seconds system-wide, she discovers the flicker was a weapon test disguised as a natural anomaly — and that her original was killed because she found proof of a prior massacre on Kepler's Reach, a colony every record insists never existed. With Earth's final transmission loop counting down to permanent erasure of the archives, Rosalind must smuggle the recovered evidence through a blockade run by the very fleet that ordered the atrocity. She broadcasts the truth in the loop's last seconds, choosing love with her copilot Idris over the duty of silence her original's handlers demanded, and the colonies finally speak again.
about_author: O. M. Thornbury is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent eleven years relaying messages between ships that had lost diplomatic contact. They write about distance, inheritance, and the people who keep signals alive when institutions would rather let them die.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV aboard the freighter Long Route as gravity flickers system-wide for nine seconds, nearly killing her and copilot Idris during a routine burn. In the aftermath, she finds a fragment of her original's hidden memory surfacing: coordinates for Kepler's Reach, a colony she has no record of. The emotional beat is disorientation — the universe itself just lied to her.

chapters.title: The Colony That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Alternating between Rosalind and Idris as they detour to the coordinates and find a sterilized ruin: forty thousand dead, scrubbed from every archive, the massacre site now a fuel depot. A surviving depot clerk recognizes Rosalind's face — her original interviewed him weeks before her murder. The beat is dread hardening into resolve; they realize inheriting the case means inheriting the target on her back.

chapters.title: The Loop Runs Down
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV under pursuit by Admiral Vess's blockade fleet, which offers her amnesty if she surrenders the evidence and accepts that her original died of 'pilot error.' Idris urges escape; duty says broadcast, love says live. Rosalind learns Earth's transmission loop ends in six hours, after which all colonial archives purge permanently. The beat is the squeeze closing: no clean choice remains.

chapters.title: Say It Before the Silence
chapters.summary: Climax and resolution in Rosalind's POV: a suicidal run through the blockade to the relay buoy, Idris wounded but flying wing, Vess's flagship bearing down. Rosalind splices the massacre records into Earth's dying loop with nine seconds left — mirroring the flicker — and the truth propagates to every world at once. Vess's fleet fractures as crews refuse orders. The beat is grief transmuted into voice: the colonies speak again, and Rosalind chooses Idris over the silence she inherited.
